parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks traveller-facing exposures. Nationally, the 2025 executive order and Nov-2025 Supreme Court ruling make birth-sex-only passport markers operative: officers are instructed to refuse cases casting doubt on an applicant's sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered; trans travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and stranding, and eight foreign governments issued advisories. This is a universal document-mismatch exposure with litigation unresolved (no working remedy documented). Locally, the 2023 executive order imposes birth-sex facility rules, and custody is documented tier-1 harm: a trans woman celled with a male sex offender who assaulted her, with courts dismissing her claims. No state hate-crime or statewide discrimination statute names gender identity; under-19 care is banned, reaching travelling families. Mitigants: no presentation offence, marriage/adoption recognition, national employment and hate-crime protections.

entry_documents.exposure: National order and Nov-2025 ruling mandate birth-sex-only markers; officers told to refuse where sex is in doubt, fraud/lifetime-ineligibility considered; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated and stranding; eight governments issued advisories. Universal, operative exposure.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; fraud finding never automatic with limited waiver; ACLU suit pending. No state-level document rule governs a visitor's foreign/out-of-jurisdiction papers.
entry_documents.interaction: Border refusal or document doubt can cascade into detention, where birth-sex placement applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Birth-sex placement documented: transitioning trans woman housed among men, celled with a male sex offender who sexually assaulted her; judge dismissed failure-to-treat, surgery-denial and failure-to-protect claims, called injuries de minimis. Placement followed her through the system; national rescission (2018) returned placement to birth sex.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National employment/hate-crime law exists but does not govern custody placement. No individualized-placement protocol documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest (including a facility-related one) moves the traveller into this documented hostile custody practice with no demonstrated remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: 2023 governor's executive order defines sex binary at birth and backs single-sex bathrooms/changing rooms in state agencies; part of a national pattern of government-building bans. Universal exposure for an outed visitor using state buildings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Dossier records no facility-use enforcement provision or arrest in this division; the trespass arrest cited occurred elsewhere. Private venues not covered by the order on this record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility confrontation can prompt ID checks, feeding the national document-mismatch exposure.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care banned under 19 (upheld 6-1 in 2024): a trans visitor under 19 cannot obtain care, and a visitor of any age cannot obtain it for a minor in their care — direct hit for adults travelling with minors. National custody conversion-therapy policy and immigrationcustody abuse apply if federally detained.
care_services.protection: Ordinary emergency care not documented as denied; adult visitors' own HRT access not documented as restricted (open question, not a documented bar).
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can out the traveller, feeding document and custody exposures.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive order ends state recognition of trans people; national orders call care 'mutilation', direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; May-2026 counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups (though 'radical gender ideology' is never the reward criterion). 66% public supports birth-sex document listing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text disclaims targeting mere disagreement; several orders enjoined; substantial counter-opinion documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile official framing raises the probability and severity of any encounter where the traveller is identified.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-19 care ban binds the travelling family directly; school-related orders are resident-facing; name change for minors requires publication (resident rule). No minor-specific facility or border rule documented beyond the general regimes.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage and adoption recognition secure; no documented separation or custody threat to a visiting guardian.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's medical need in this division converts into the care-ban exposure for the accompanying adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-level trans violence statistics sourced; national bias data shows sustained anti-LGBTQ hate incidence; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes and this division's 1997 hate-crime law does not name it.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity since 2009; Bostock employment protection; no sodomy law (repealed 1978); no documented police targeting of trans people here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State silence on bias motive shifts reliance to national charging, which is documented but unevenly used.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National passport, order-based regimes in unresolved litigation with no documented relief; custody claims dismissed; no statewide discrimination or GI hate-crime statute; one city ordinance repealed by petition.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning national courts have blocked/enjoined several orders; pending ACLU suit; legal-aid FAQ maintained; local ordinances and college policy provide patchy cover.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists nationally but has not altered the operative document or custody practices the traveller meets.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier: like Veluna, this jurisdiction has an operative birth-sex facility rule with no visitor exemption and no demonstrated relief, plus polite-but-unaccepting social texture. It sits slightly below 0.35-A because it adds a nationwide document regime producing refusals and stranding, and documented custody sexual assault with judicial dismissal — exposures Veluna's profile does not carry.

Higher than this case: Veleda's worst feature is invasive transport searches persisting after reviews, with no custody-assault record and accepting residents. Here the national marker regime threatens entry refusal/lifetime fraud findings, plus birth-sex custody with a documented sexual assault dismissed by courts — two universal or tier-1 exposures rather than one.

Materially higher: Ilvora has acceptance, an enforced compensation order for a trans traveller, identity-based ward practice, and only a dead-letter statute plus an open custody question. This jurisdiction documents the opposite on the heaviest axes — unmatchable documents, facility exclusion, hostile custody — so it cannot reach the 0.75 tier despite marriage recognition and national protections.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a national document regime (operative since Nov 2025) that makes birth-sex markers unavoidable and lets officers refuse entry where sex is doubted, layered on a division whose 2023 executive order imposes birth-sex facility rules and whose courts dismissed a trans prisoner's claims after she was sexually assaulted in a men's prison. These interact — a facility or service encounter can trigger an ID check, which feeds the border mismatch exposure, which if it ends in detention reaches the documented birth-sex custody practice with no working remedy. Adults travelling with minors additionally face the under-19 care ban. Countervailing facts are real but weaker: no presentation offence, marriage/adoption recognition, national employment and hate-crime coverage, and litigation that has blocked some orders without yet changing documents, facilities, or custody.
